## Steps

### 1. Review Board State

Parse the pre-loaded board data above. Identify:
- All items with `status: backlog` or `status: current` (candidates for completion)
- Epics and their child tasks (via `parent` field)
- Blocked items and their blockers
- Items with terminal status (`done`, `processed`) that should be archived
- Items missing a required `status` field (all types except `reference`)

### 2. Gather Codebase Context

- Run `git log --oneline` for recent commits (last 30) to understand what work has been done
- Only Read full file bodies for tasks whose status is `backlog` or `current` AND whose title suggests overlap with recent commits
- Use the context budget escalation (Glob → Grep → Read with limit → Full read) for any additional lookups

### 3. Detect Completed Work

For each task with `status: backlog` or `status: current`, check if the work described has already been done:

- Look at recent commits for evidence the work was completed
- Check the codebase for the feature/fix the task describes
- If the work is done, flag it for status update to `done`

### 4. Detect New Work Needed

Scan for things that should become tasks but aren't tracked yet:

- Check recent commits for TODOs or FIXMEs introduced in code
- Look at open epics — are there obvious next steps not yet captured as tasks?
- Check if any `blocked_by` dependencies have been resolved (unblocking tasks)

### 5. Update Epic Progress

For each active epic:

- Check if all child tasks are `done` — if so, flag the epic as `done`
- Check if any child tasks are `current` — if so, the epic should be `current`
- Update the task list in the epic body if tasks have been added/removed

### 6. Check for Stale Items

- Tasks marked `current` but with no related commits in the last 30 days
- Epics in `planning` with no child tasks
- Resources stuck in `inbox` or `processing`

### 7. Present Changes

Present ALL proposed changes as a single summary before making any edits:

```
## Board Update Proposal

### Status Changes → Archive
- TASK-0003: backlog → done → **archive** (cache-decoded-image: implemented in commit a1b2c3d)
- EPIC-0001: planning → current (has active child tasks)
- NOTE-0002: already processed → **archive**

### New Tasks Suggested
- "Fix FIXME in preprocessing.rs line 42" (found in recent commit)

### Missing Status
- TASK-0025: no status field (required for tasks)

### Stale Items
- TASK-0007: marked current but no activity in 45 days

### Unblocked
- TASK-0005: blocker TASK-0003 is now done
```

**Terminal-status items must be archived atomically.** When a status change results in a terminal status (`done` for tasks/epics, `processed` for resources/notes), the archiving step is bundled into the same proposal line — not presented as a separate action. Items already at a terminal status but not yet archived should also appear with an **archive** tag.

ADRs are the sole exception — they are never archived regardless of status.

**Avoid redundant invocations** — if this skill was already invoked earlier in the session and the board has not been modified since, reuse the previous board data instead of invoking again.

Ask the user to approve, reject, or cherry-pick which changes to apply. Then execute only the approved changes:

- **Status updates + archive**: For items reaching a terminal status, update the status field first, then immediately run `bash "/Users/grant/.claude/plugins/cache/gdkeller/board/0.1.0/scripts/archive-batch.sh" ./board <file>` in the same step. Never leave an item with a terminal status outside `archive/`.
- **Status updates (non-terminal)**: Use `/board:board-edit` to update status fields
- **New tasks**: Invoke `/board:board-add` for each approved new task
- **Archive-only** (items already at terminal status): Run `bash "/Users/grant/.claude/plugins/cache/gdkeller/board/0.1.0/scripts/archive-batch.sh" ./board <file1> <file2> ...` directly

# TASK-0110: Tokenize hardcoded colors in target-color components

Eliminate hardcoded color values in target-color components flagged in PR #5 review.

> **Paths refreshed 2026-10-20.** The component flatten (e3b8ab6) replaced the old `components/target/` directory with `components/TargetSwatch/`, `components/TargetFormats/`, and `components/FormatSelector/`. `ColorInput` is no longer a separate component — it is a local function inside `TargetSwatch.tsx`.

## Scope

Offenders confirmed in current code (2026-10-20):

- `FormatSelector/FormatSelector.tsx` — `btnActive` uses `text-white` → `text-text-primary` (or appropriate token).
- `TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`, swatch trigger `boxShadow` — inline `rgba(255,255,255,0.1)` / `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)` / `rgba(255,255,255,0.15)` → token-based shadow.
- `TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`, `ColorInput` invalid state — `border-red-500`. No error/invalid token exists in `@theme` yet; add a semantic one (e.g. `--color-border-invalid`) rather than reaching for a Tailwind palette color.
- `TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`, canvas crosshair — `ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(0,0,0,0.4)"`. Canvas can't consume Tailwind classes; read the token via `getComputedStyle` or a shared constant sourced from the theme.
- `TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`, active-ring color `hsl(${targetHue}, 80%, 55%)` — derived from the user's hue, so arguably content rather than chrome. Decide explicitly and leave a comment either way.

## Acceptance

- Grep for `text-white`, `rgba(`, `-red-`, hex literals, and hsl literals across `app/src/components/{TargetSwatch,TargetFormats,FormatSelector}/**` returns no unexplained offenders.
- Visual parity preserved (or intentional improvement noted).

## Intentional visual changes

Noted 2026-10-30, for commits 3e17daa and 936d97d plus the token follow-up.

- **Swatch trigger outer rings are dimmer.** They used to be translucent white over the bar: `rgba(255,255,255,0.15)`, about 21% L, and `0.1` when drifted, about 13% L after the swatch's 0.6 opacity. They are now opaque `border-elevated` (15%) and `border-default` (12%). The 2px `surface-base` gap still separates the swatch from the bar, so nothing breaks. Getting the old brightness back would need a new border token, and the existing border names (default/elevated) describe elevation, not intensity. So we accepted the dimmer ring instead.
- **The drifted swatch's inset edge is slightly darker.** It went from `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)` to `--color-stroke-halo` (0.4 alpha), which it shares with the picker crosshair halo.
- **The active-target ring stays a literal**, with a comment explaining that it is content, not chrome. TASK-0124 covers whether it should match the actual target color.

## Source

- NOTE-0030

# TASK-0111: Fix target-color a11y gaps

PR #5 review surfaced several accessibility gaps in target-color components.

> **Partially resolved — refreshed 2026-10-20.** Commit 7dc1bed (keyboard a11y for the picker) already landed some of the original scope. Verified state below.

## Already done

- ~~**`aria-label`** on icon-only controls~~ — clear button has `aria-label="Clear target color"`.
- Canvas picker has `focus-visible` outline, `role="application"` with keyboard instructions, and a `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` readout.

## Remaining scope

- **Clear button focus visibility** — it is `opacity-0` and only revealed by `group-hover:opacity-100`, so keyboard focus lands on an invisible control. Reveal it on focus (`focus-visible:opacity-100` / `group-focus-within:opacity-100`) and add a `focus-visible` ring.
- **ColorInput focus** — currently `outline-none` with only a `focus:border-text-faint` border shift. Replace with a proper `focus-visible` ring that meets 3:1 non-text contrast.
- **`aria-live`** for the TargetFormats display — it has `aria-label="Target color formats"` but no live region, so screen readers aren't told when the target changes or drifts.

## Acceptance

- Keyboard-only flow through target-color UI is fully visible and announced.
- Axe / Lighthouse a11y audit passes for target-color components.

# TASK-0113: Extend oklch regex to accept slash-alpha syntax

The current OKLCH parser doesn't accept the CSS Color Level 4 slash-alpha syntax: `oklch(70% 0.15 240 / 50%)`. Users pasting modern CSS values get rejected.

## Acceptance

- Regex / parser accepts `L C H` and `L C H / A` forms.
- Alpha is parsed as percentage or 0–1 number.
- Existing well-formed inputs continue to parse identically.
- Parser tests cover slash-alpha cases.

# TASK-0115: Fix opacity-55 contrast degradation in TargetFormats drifted state

When the target is "drifted" (user has moved hue/sat sliders away from the target value), TargetFormats dims its display via `opacity-55`. That blends unpredictably with the surface color and fails contrast in dark mode. This violates the project rule: never use opacity for text dimming — use explicit dim tokens.

## Acceptance

- Drifted state uses an explicit text token (e.g., `text-text-faint`) instead of opacity.
- Drifted readout meets WCAG AA on the project's dark surface.
- Visual hierarchy still distinguishes drifted from active state.

## Source

- NOTE-0030

## Related

- Project convention: no `white/N` opacity-on-text patterns (`feedback_no_opacity_text`).

# TASK-0122: Fix target picker canvas rendering blank when popover opens

Clicking the target swatch opens the popover, but the hue × saturation picker canvas is an empty dark square. It only appears after you click inside the area where it should be.

## Reproduce

1. Open the app (reproduces on the live site, which matches `main`).
2. Click the target swatch next to the Hue slider.
3. **Actual:** the popover shows "Hue / Sat" readouts and the color input, but the 200×200 canvas above them is blank.
4. **Expected:** the full hue/saturation gradient with the crosshair at the current position, on first paint.

It happens on **every** open, not just the first, because the popover content unmounts when it closes.

## Impact

- The picker looks broken on every open.
- The only way to reveal it destroys state. Mouse-down on the canvas calls `pickFromCoords()`, which runs `clearTarget()` and sets hue/saturation to the clicked point. Arrow keys on the focused canvas do the same. **A user with an active target color can't see the picker without wiping their target.**

## Root cause

`TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`:

- The canvas lives inside `<Popover.Portal><Popover.Content>` (lines ~321–337). Radix unmounts that content while the popover is closed.
- Drawing happens in an effect keyed only on `drawPicker`, which changes only when `hue` / `saturation` change (lines ~193–195):
  ```ts
  useEffect(() => {
    if (canvasRef.current) drawPicker(canvasRef.current);
  }, [drawPicker]);
  ```
- When the popover opens, the canvas mounts but `drawPicker` hasn't changed, so the effect doesn't re-run and nothing is drawn. Clicking the canvas changes hue/saturation, which changes `drawPicker`, so the effect fires and the canvas finally paints.

**Regression from 7dc1bed (2026-04-17, "fix stale crosshair" — a PR #5 review fix).** The original implementation (ab4cb01) used a callback ref that drew whenever the canvas attached (`canvasRef.current = canvas; if (canvas) drawPicker(canvas);`). 7dc1bed swapped it for `useRef` + the effect above, which fixed the crosshair-update case but lost draw-on-mount. It has been live since the Apr 17 deploy.

## Fix options

1. **Recommended: extract the canvas into its own component** (e.g. `HueSatPicker.tsx` inside `TargetSwatch/`), with its own `useEffect` that draws on mount and whenever `hue` / `saturation` change. Mounting now coincides with the popover opening, so both cases are covered without extra state. It's also the natural home for TASK-0112 (Pointer Events), and it shrinks `TargetSwatch.tsx`.
2. **Restore a memoized callback ref** that draws on attach (`useCallback((node) => { canvasRef.current = node; if (node) drawPicker(node); }, [drawPicker])`), alongside or instead of the effect. Before choosing this, confirm what "stale crosshair" bug 7dc1bed was fixing so it doesn't come back.
3. **Controlled `open` state** on `Popover.Root`, with `open` added to the draw effect's dependencies.

Avoid `forceMount`. Keeping a hidden canvas mounted just to work around the lifecycle adds visibility/focus handling for no benefit.

**Optional, while here:** the gradient never depends on hue/saturation, only the crosshair does. Building the 200×200 `ImageData` once (memo or module-level) and redrawing just the crosshair avoids a 40k-pixel loop on every drag tick.

## Acceptance

- The canvas is fully rendered on first paint in each of these cases:
  - first open
  - reopen
  - reopen after hue/saturation were changed via the sliders while the popover was closed
  - reopen with an active target
- The crosshair still tracks changes while the popover is open, from the sliders, canvas drag, arrow keys, and applying a target via the input. This was the case 7dc1bed fixed.
- Opening the popover never changes hue, saturation, or the target.

## Verification

There's no test runner in the project, so verify in the browser (Playwright works). After opening the popover, sample the canvas without interacting with it:

```js
const c = document.querySelector('[role=dialog] canvas, [data-radix-popper-content-wrapper] canvas');
c.getContext('2d').getImageData(100, 100, 1, 1).data[3]; // expect 255, not 0
```

Repeat after closing and reopening, and after moving the Hue slider while closed.

`.screenshots/mono-2-popover.png` (captured 2026-10-20 on the live site) shows the blank canvas, and `mono-3-target-active.png` shows it painted after a target was applied, which changed hue/saturation and so triggered a draw.

## Related

- TASK-0112: Pointer Events / touch for the same canvas (do both in the extracted component)
- TASK-0111: target-color a11y gaps (the canvas's keyboard and focus behavior)
- TASK-0110: tokenize the canvas crosshair `rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` stroke

+import { test } from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { formatTargetColor, parseTargetColor } from "./colors.ts";
+
+test("oklch parses with and without slash-alpha", () => {
+  const base = { hue: 201, saturation: 0.88, format: "oklch" };
+  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetColor("oklch(70% 0.15 240)"), base);
+  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetColor("oklch(0.7 0.15 240)"), base);
+  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetColor("oklch(70% 0.15 240 / 50%)"), base);
+  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetColor("oklch(0.7 0.15 240/0.5)"), base);
+  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetColor("OKLCH(70% 0.15 240)"), base);
+});
+
+test("achromatic oklch has zero saturation", () => {
+  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetColor("oklch(1 0 0)"), {
+    hue: 0,
+    saturation: 0,
+    format: "oklch",
+  });
+});
+
+test("malformed input is rejected", () => {
+  assert.equal(parseTargetColor("oklch(0.7 0.15 240 / )"), null);
+  assert.equal(parseTargetColor("oklch(0.7 0.15)"), null);
+  assert.equal(parseTargetColor("nope"), null);
+  assert.equal(parseTargetColor("  "), null);
+});
+
+test("hsl/rgb output is spaced and round-trips", () => {
+  assert.equal(formatTargetColor(180, 0.5, "hsl"), "hsl(180, 50%, 50%)");
+  assert.equal(formatTargetColor(180, 0.5, "rgb"), "rgb(64, 191, 191)");
+  for (const format of ["hsl", "rgb"] as const) {
+    assert.deepEqual(parseTargetColor(formatTargetColor(180, 0.5, format)), {
+      hue: 180,
+      saturation: 0.5,
+      format,
+    });
+  }
+  assert.deepEqual(parseTargetColor("RGB(64, 191, 191)"), {
+    hue: 180,
+    saturation: 0.5,
+    format: "rgb",
+  });
+});

---
type: epic
status: planning
created: 2026-04-06
---

# EPIC-0014: Target color input UX refinements

Users enter a color (e.g., `#FF5733`) into the target picker, but the app extracts only hue + saturation and forces lightness to 50%. The swatch then shows a different hex value, which is confusing — users reasonably wonder "I put in this hex value, why am I seeing a different one?" The "H+S at L50" explanation is small and buried inside a popover with no persistent indicator, and the same confusion extends to HSL and OKLCH displays.

## Goals

- Make the L50 normalization obvious with clear before/after display of the user's input alongside the resulting working color
- Show a persistent "target active" indicator outside the popover so users can see at a glance that they entered a target
- Display the working color in all four formats (hex, rgb, hsl, oklch) inline so users can verify the identity and copy any representation
- Support a "drift" model: when users move hue/sat sliders after entering a target, the indicator goes stale rather than silently vanishing

## Scope

- **Move target state to Zustand** — target fields (`targetInput`, `targetFormat`, `targetHue`, `targetSat`) move from local TargetSwatch state to `paletteStore.ts` so `ControlBar` can render the inline multi-format display without prop drilling
- **Arrow notation in popover** — replace "Input"/"H+S at L50" with `#FF5733 → #BF4040` and annotation "hue + saturation at L50"
- **Persistent target indicator** — swatch trigger shows chromatic ring when target is active, dimmed/dotted when drifted, clear (X) button on hover
- **Inline multi-format display** — new `TargetFormats` component in ControlBar showing hex/rgb/hsl/oklch with click-to-copy when target is active
- **`formatAllFormats()` utility** — compose existing formatters to return `{ hex, rgb, hsl, oklch }` for a given hue/sat at L50

## Deferred

Slider-locking (TASK-0055, TASK-0056) was originally in scope to prevent accidental target invalidation, but it pre-emptively solves a problem users don't actually report and risks making the controls feel constrained. Dropping it in favor of the clarity-focused work above. Revisit only if real usage shows users losing targets by accident.

# TASK-0123: Token focus ring on target trigger; fix clear-button hit area and touch visibility

Two problems that predate this task, both in `TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`. The review of the TASK-0110/0111 work (commit 3e17daa) found them.

## Trigger focus ring

The swatch trigger button has no focus styles, so it shows Chrome's default `auto` outline, which is blue (rgb(0, 95, 204)).

- When the target is blue, the active-target ring is a similar blue (e.g. rgb(48, 110, 232)). "Focused" and "target active" then look almost the same.
- The outline is chrome that has color, which breaks "colors are the content".
- It draws as a rectangle around both the swatch and the hex label, and the × overlaps its corner.

Fix: put `outline-none` on the button and draw the ring on the round swatch instead: `group-focus-visible:outline-2 group-focus-visible:outline-offset-2 group-focus-visible:outline-text-primary`. This matches the canvas and input rings.

## Clear (×) button

- It is 16×16 px, below the 24px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8 and the project rule). It also overlaps the trigger, so the 2.5.8 spacing exception doesn't apply.
- It only becomes visible on hover. In the built CSS, `group-hover:opacity-100` sits inside `@media (hover: hover)`, so touch users never see it. The invisible `opacity-0` button can still be tapped, which leaves a hidden spot on the swatch's corner that silently clears the target.
- Its focus ring (2px outline, 2px offset) is heavy on a 16px circle and cuts into the swatch.

Fix: give it a 24px hit area (`size-6` wrapping the 16px circle), add `pointer-coarse:opacity-100`, and use `outline-offset-1`. Another option is a visible "Clear" text button in the TargetFormats row.

## Acceptance

- Keyboard focus on the trigger shows a neutral, token-based ring around the swatch. No browser-default outline.
- The clear button has a hit area of at least 24px and is visible on touch devices.
- No visual regression for mouse users.

## Source

- Review of commit 3e17daa (2026-10-30): visual UX and a11y reviewers.
### tasks/TASK-0124_derive-active-target-ring-from-target-color.md
---

# TASK-0124: Derive the active-target ring from the actual target color

When a target is active and hasn't drifted, the swatch trigger's ring is `hsl(targetHue, 80%, 55%)` (`TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx`, `ringColor`). Saturation is fixed at 80%, so a nearly gray target (for example `hsl(220, 5%, 50%)`) gets a vivid blue ring that doesn't represent it.

The code comment calls the ring "content, not chrome". That only holds if the ring actually shows the target color.

## Options

- Use the real target color, `hsl(targetHue, targetSat, 50%)`. Very gray targets would get a ring that barely contrasts with the swatch, so check how that looks.
- Use a neutral `text-primary` ring and treat it as chrome. That is simpler and consistent, but loses the color cue.

## Acceptance

- The ring for a low-saturation target no longer suggests a saturated color.
- Update the comment on `ringColor` to match whichever option is chosen.

## Source

- Review of commit 3e17daa (2026-10-30): visual UX reviewer.
### tasks/TASK-0125_keep-picker-crosshair-visible-at-edges.md

# TASK-0125: Keep the picker crosshair visible at the canvas edges and on light hues

The hue × saturation crosshair in `TargetSwatch/TargetSwatch.tsx` (`drawPicker`) has two legibility problems. Both predate this task.

- **Clipped at the edges.** At saturation 100%, which covers any pure brand color, only half the circle is drawn. At hue 0, only a quarter is drawn.
- **Low contrast on light hues.** Over yellow, cyan and green, neither ring reaches 3:1 against the gradient (WCAG 1.4.11). On yellow, the white ring is 1.03:1 and the dark halo is 2.83:1.

## Fix options

- Inset the gradient by about 6px, or clamp the crosshair center so the full circle stays inside the canvas.
- Make the outer halo thicker, or raise `--color-stroke-halo` alpha to about 0.6. Check what that does to the drifted swatch's inset edge, which uses the same token.
- Optional, from TASK-0122: the gradient never depends on hue or saturation. Build the `ImageData` once and redraw only the crosshair.

## Acceptance

- The crosshair is fully visible at every hue/saturation, including 0°, 360°, 0% and 100%.
- At least one of the two rings reaches 3:1 against the gradient underneath it.

## Related

- TASK-0112: Pointer Events and touch support for the same canvas.

## Source

- Review of commit 3e17daa (2026-10-30): visual UX and a11y reviewers.

# TASK-0126: Stop layout shift when copying a value in TargetFormats

Clicking a value in the TARGET formats row (`TargetFormats/TargetFormats.tsx`) replaces it with "Copied". The button shrinks, and every value after it slides left. At 1280px, the RGB button goes from 144px to 77px, and HSL and OKLCH move 67px left. This predates this task.

The values also change length while you drag Hue or Saturation, so the row jitters during a drag.

## Fix options

- Stack "Copied" over the value in a single grid cell (`grid` with both children in `[grid-area:1/1]`) and make the value `invisible` while "Copied" shows. The button then keeps the value's width.
- Fixed-width value cells, sized to the longest string for each format.

## Acceptance

- Copying a value doesn't move any other element in the row.
- Dragging the sliders doesn't reflow the row at lg widths.

## Related

- TASK-0102: Redesign the swatch copy-feedback overlay (the same problem on palette swatches).
- TASK-0121: A mono typeface for color values would fix some of the width jitter.

## Source

- Review of commit 3e17daa (2026-10-30): visual UX reviewer.
### tasks/TASK-0127_controlbar-translucency-breaks-faint-text-contrast.md
---
type: task

created: 2026-10-30
parent: EPIC-0021

# TASK-0127: Fix faint-text contrast under the translucent ControlBar

`ControlBar` is `bg-surface-raised/85 backdrop-blur-xl sticky`. With the page scrolled to the top, the bar works out to about #121212, and `text-text-faint` (55%) reaches about 5.5:1. When light palette swatches scroll underneath it, the 15% that shows through brightens the bar.

- Over white swatches (the default `lMax=100` produces them), the bar is about #373737 and `text-faint` drops to **3.53:1**, which fails WCAG 1.4.3.
- Over an L90 gray, it is 3.73:1.

This affects every `text-faint` label in the bar: the slider labels, the TARGET row labels, and "Target (drifted)". This predates this task.

`scripts/contrast-audit.mjs` only checks opaque surfaces, so it misses this case.

## Fix options

- Raise the bar's opacity: `bg-surface-raised/95` brings `text-faint` to about 4.86:1 in the worst case.
- Or use `text-text-muted` for any label that can sit over scrolled content.

## Acceptance

- Every text token used in ControlBar meets AA (4.5:1), even with white swatches directly underneath.
- Optional: teach `contrast-audit.mjs` to model the translucent bar over a white backdrop.

## Source

- Review of commit 3e17daa (2026-10-30): a11y reviewer.
### tasks/TASK-0128_formatselector-active-button-dims-on-hover.md
---
type: task
status: backlog
priority: 3
created: 2026-10-30
parent: EPIC-0021

# TASK-0128: Stop the FormatSelector active button dimming on hover

In `FormatSelector/FormatSelector.tsx`, `btnBase` includes `text-text-muted hover:text-text-secondary`, and `btnActive` adds `text-text-primary`. Two problems follow:

- **It dims on hover.** The active button still has the base `hover:text-text-secondary`, so hovering it drops the text from 98% to 85% lightness.
- **The active color is fragile.** `text-text-primary` only wins over `text-text-muted` because Tailwind happens to emit `.text-text-primary` later in the CSS. Change the order and the active button silently turns muted.

## Fix

Keep the color classes separate from the shared base:

- the shared base has no text color;
- the inactive state gets `text-text-muted hover:text-text-secondary`;
- the active state gets `text-text-primary`.

Another option is `cn()` (tailwind-merge), if the project adopts it.

## Acceptance

- The active button stays `text-primary` when hovered.
- The active and inactive color classes never appear on the same element.

## Source

- Review of commit 3e17daa (2026-10-30): a11y reviewer.
